localSignup.description: User creates an account using username, email, and password.
steps: Express route builds a new User doc from req.body
User.register(user, password) called directly — passport-local-mongoose's built-in helper, no workaround needed (unlike login, which bypasses passport.authenticate('local') — see platformQuirks)
Password hashed and User document created in MongoDB
Server returns token and normalized user object

localLogin.description: User logs in with username and password.
steps: Cloud Functions pre-parses the request body, breaking passport-local-mongoose's stream-based authenticate() — passport.authenticate('local') is bypassed
User manually fetched from MongoDB with .select('+hash +salt')
Password verified by calling the instance method user.authenticate(password, callback) directly
Server returns token and normalized user object

googleOAuth.description: User logs in with Google account.
steps: Passport redirects user to Google login page
Server searches for existing user by googleId
If not found, new user is created using profile data
Server redirects to frontend /oauth-success with token
platformNotes: Requires an absolute callbackURL via the GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL env var, because of the Cloud Functions path prefix
Requires middleware to parse req.query from req.url, since req.query otherwise arrives undefined on Cloud Functions

platformQuirks.description: Cloud Functions pre-parses incoming HTTP bodies before Express/Passport middleware runs, which would consume the request stream that passport.authenticate('local') needs to read itself.
platformQuirks.mitigation: Login bypasses the affected stream-based Passport helper: it manually loads the user (.select('+hash +salt')) and calls user.authenticate(password, callback) directly instead of passport.authenticate('local'). Signup does not need a workaround — User.register() doesn't depend on reading the request stream the way passport.authenticate('local') does, so it's called directly.

steps: Client sends request with Authorization header

securityConsiderations: Admin-only access for user management routes
Mongoose NoSQL injection CVE patched (dependency audit)
middleware.js/placeRouter.js query construction reviewed 2026-09-14 — low risk (see architecture-map.json stack.security)
GET /users/:userId restricted to admins (fixed 2026-09-14 — previously any authenticated user could look up any other user's full profile)
